title: autopilot ledger removal, final step: review launch is decided from the jobs it already records, and the once() write-ahead ledger, its actions map and the per-class migration flags are deleted
acceptance: Why. After T-190, T-193, T-200 and T-204, `launch_review` is the last caller of the write-ahead `once()` ledger (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:313-318 calls `self.once(['launch-review', pr['number'], pr['head']['sha']], …)`; `once` is bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:233-246, `recover()`'s actions branch :248-253). The jobs map already records every review child (`start_job`, fm_autopilot_loop.py:265-287; `consume_jobs` :289-301; `recover_jobs` :303-311), so the ledger only duplicates it, and an action that reaches 'uncertain' blocks that head's review forever. Four one-time migration blocks (`migrated_t190`, `migrated_t193`, `migrated_t200`, `migrated_t204`, fm_autopilot.py:67-107) exist only to drain the ledger class by class. T-203's reload idle check also reads it (`reload_due`, fm_autopilot.py:855-862: `not any(a.get('state') == 'started' for a in pilot.data['actions'].values())`).

Job records name what they run. `start_job` (fm_autopilot_loop.py:265-287) stores, in addition to today's `task`, `state` and `path`, the fields `kind` (its first argument), `number` (`pr['number']`) and `head` (`pr['head']['sha']`) in `data['jobs'][identity]`, for every kind. Nothing else about `start_job` changes: identity formula, packet file, `life.start(..., owner=os.getpid())`, the completion thread and the exceptions it raises (T-193's `advance` relies on them for its retry series) stay as they are. A helper `job_for(kind, number, head)` (on `MechanicalLoop`) returns the first job record matching all three, comparing `number` as an int; for a record without `kind` (written before this change) it reads the packet at `job['path']` (its `kind`, `pr.number`, `pr.head.sha`), and a packet that is missing or unreadable does not match.

Review launch without the ledger. `launch_review(task, pr, round_number=1)` (fm_autopilot_loop.py:313-318), in order: (1) if `job_for('review', pr['number'], pr['head']['sha'])` exists in any state (running, consuming, done or uncertain), return without starting or waking: a running one is in progress, a done one already reported its outcome through `job_completed`, an uncertain one already queued its wake (`consume_jobs`, `recover_jobs` or step (2) below). This is exactly today's rule that a head gets at most one autopilot-launched review; no verdict-based skip is added, because gate 7 can still ask for review at the same head for reasons a new round fixes (an unsigned approval, a spec, contract or conventions hash changed after it, a review source that no longer verifies: bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:355-378). (2) otherwise, inside one try block catching (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError), compute `verdict_before=key(self.verdict(task))` and call `start_job('review', task, pr, <today's fm-review.sh argv>, verdict_before=...)` exactly as today. On any of those exceptions, raised by `self.verdict`, by `start_job` before it writes its record (`path.parent.mkdir` :271, `save_json` :272) or after (`life.start` :277-278): if `job_for('review', number, head)` finds a record in state 'running' with no `.result.json` beside its non-empty path, set it to 'uncertain'; if it finds none, write `data['jobs'][key(['review-launch', number, head])] = dict(kind='review', task=task, number=number, head=head, state='uncertain', path='')`; then queue one wake with identity `review-launch-<number>-<head>` naming the task, English 'Review launch failed at <first 12 of head>: <error>; launch it by hand or fix the cause' and Chinese '審查啟動失敗：<error>；請手動啟動或排除原因', save, and return without raising. The gate job that called it is therefore consumed as done (not uncertain), no 'running' review record without a child is left to block T-203's reload drain, and every later gate exit 7 at that head matches step (1): no retry and no second wake. `job_for` never reads a packet for a record that has `kind` (so path '' is fine), and `consume_jobs`/`recover_jobs` act only on 'running'/'consuming' records, so an 'uncertain' record with path '' is never opened.

Delete the ledger. Remove `Pilot.once` (fm_autopilot.py:233-246), the actions loop in `Pilot.recover` (:248-253; the T-204 `restacks` sweep at :254-255 stays and `recover()` keeps its name and its caller at :998), the `actions={}` default (:63-65) and every read of `self.data['actions']`. `reload_due` (fm_autopilot.py:855-862) drops its `actions` clause; it stays idle-gated on jobs running or consuming, batches and unpushed wakes exactly as T-203 defined, and design §15.8 and docs/autopilot.md say 'started actions' no longer exist. `data['jobs']`'s own 'uncertain' state, `consume_jobs`, `recover_jobs` and the 'job-<id>' wakes are unchanged. The module docstring (bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py:8-10, 'Other side effects remain write-ahead until firstmate reconciles an ambiguous crash.') becomes: 'No write-ahead action ledger remains: each step is re-decided from per-PR records and observed state, and only owned jobs interrupted mid-run are left for firstmate to reconcile.'

One migration replaces four. Delete the `migrated_t190`, `migrated_t193`, `migrated_t200` and `migrated_t204` blocks (fm_autopilot.py:67-107) and replace them, in the same place in `Pilot.__init__` (before `tracking_started` and `legacy_ask_records`, so before `serve()` calls `recover()`), with one upgrade guarded by `migrated_t205`. `jobs` is not among the defaults at :63-65 and is created lazily: the migration calls `self.data.setdefault('jobs', {})` only at the moment it converts a launch-review action into a review record, so a state.json without `actions`, or whose actions convert nothing, gains only `migrated_t205`. Every identity is read as `action.get('identity') or []`. When `data` has an `actions` key it walks every action and, by `identity[0]`: 'update', 'advance', 'restack', 'recheck', 'observed-merge': delete the action and pop its undelivered wake `'autopilot-' + key([ctx['project'], 'action-' + token])` (exactly what the old per-class blocks did); 'pr-event': the T-200 rule unchanged (a not-done `['pr-event', n, 'merged'|'closed']` whose `data['pulls'][str(n)]` is terminal gets `event_pending`), then delete and pop the undelivered wake; 'launch-review' and any other or missing identity: state 'done' is deleted with its undelivered wake popped; state 'started' (an interruption the old `recover()` would have reported) is deleted and, unless its 'action-<token>' wake already exists, queues that wake with today's recover text ('Autopilot stopped during an action; reconcile its outcome' / '自動駕駛於步驟執行中停止；請核對結果') using `self.queue('action-' + token, …)`; state 'uncertain' is deleted and its existing wake, delivered or not, is left in `data['wakes']` untouched so it is still pushed. To keep the one-review-per-head block that a not-done launch-review action gave under old code: for a well-formed `['launch-review', n, head]` action (int n, 40-hex head) in state 'started' or 'uncertain', when `job_for('review', n, head)` finds no record, the migration writes `data['jobs'][key(['review-launch', n, head])] = dict(kind='review', task=<action task>, number=n, head=head, state='uncertain', path='')`, the same record acceptance 3 writes for a failed start, so the next gate exit 7 at that head starts nothing. A malformed launch-review identity writes no record (it never matched a head). Then delete the `actions` key and set `migrated_t205`. Files already under state/wake-queue/ stay byte-identical. The old `migrated_t190`/`t193`/`t200`/`t204` keys already in state.json are neither read nor removed. A second startup changes nothing and queues nothing.

Tests, all under tests/** (each file stays under 1200 lines: autopilot_cases.py is 956, autopilot_loop.py 728, autopilot_sync.py 332, autopilot_reload.py 394, autopilot_jobs.py checked before editing):
- Review launch (tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py): the `start_job` stub at :39 (and its copies at :157 and :593) also writes `self.pilot.data['jobs'][<n>] = dict(kind=kind, task=task, number=pr['number'], head=pr['head']['sha'], state='running', path=...)` for kind 'review', so `test_worker_head_runs_gates_then_review` (:78-85, a second gate exit 7 launches no second review) keeps passing. New cases: a done, uncertain or consuming review job at the head starts nothing and queues nothing; a review job at a different head does not block; a legacy job record without `kind` matches through its packet file and a missing packet does not match; a verdict bound to the same head whose binding is stale (the test's `verdict` stub returns a row at the PR head) still launches the review on gate exit 7, as today; a `start_job` stub that writes its record and then raises (each of the four exception types) leaves that record 'uncertain'; a stub that raises before writing any record, and a `verdict` stub that raises, each leave one 'uncertain' record keyed `key(['review-launch', n, head])` with path ''; in every failure case exactly one `review-launch-<n>-<head>` wake is queued, nothing is raised, and a second gate exit 7 at that head starts nothing and queues nothing more; a later `consume_jobs()` and `recover_jobs()` leave the path-'' record untouched.
- Real `start_job` (tests/lib/autopilot_jobs.py:40 area): the stored record carries `kind`, `number` and `head`.
- Migration (tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py): replace `test_restack_migration_drops_all_legacy_states_once` (:311), `test_update_migration_preserves_delivered_files_across_two_startups` (:795), `test_event_recheck_migration_removes_all_states_before_recovery_once` (:822) and `test_advance_migration_removes_all_states_before_recovery_once` (:873) with T-205 migration cases that seed one action of every class in each of 'started', 'done' and 'uncertain', one delivered and one undelivered wake per class, and a terminal PR with a not-done pr-event: after startup, `recover()` and `flush()` there is no `actions` key, `migrated_t205` is set, the per-class undelivered wakes are gone, the terminal PR has `event_pending`, a started launch-review has exactly one queued reconcile wake, an uncertain launch-review keeps its wake, delivered files are byte-identical, and a second startup leaves state.json and the wake queue unchanged; a state.json with no `actions` key (and no `jobs` key) gains only `migrated_t205`: no `jobs` key is created and nothing else changes; a state.json whose actions convert no launch-review likewise gains no `jobs` key. A case seeds actions with a malformed identity (`['launch-review']`, `['launch-review', 'x', 'short']`) and with a missing or empty identity, each in 'started' and in 'uncertain': no jobs record is written for any of them, each 'started' one gets exactly one reconcile `action-<token>` wake, and each 'uncertain' one keeps its existing wake unchanged. A case seeds a started and an uncertain well-formed `['launch-review', 12, HEAD]` action (with no review job) and, after the migration, gate exit 7 at HEAD starts no review and queues no `review-launch` wake (only the reconcile wake for the started one); a launch-review action whose head already has a review job writes no second record. The negative T-200 cases of the replaced event/recheck test are kept: a 'done' pr-event sets no `event_pending` (tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:858), a non-terminal pulls entry is not marked (pull 99, :860), and a missing pulls entry is not created (pull 98, :859). The default checks of the replaced advance and restack tests are kept: a popped `advanced` (:886-890) and a popped `restacks` (:324, :327) each return as their default after restart. The upgrade-defaults check carried by the replaced update-migration test (tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py:806-811: remove `poll_seq`, `retries`, `holds` and `updates` from state.json, restart, and see each return as its default) is kept in the new migration cases. tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py:553 (`test_parked_advance_migrates_and_equal_ref_gates_once`) and tests/lib/autopilot_sync.py:206 (`test_migration_repairs_missing_terminal_event_on_next_poll`) seed `actions` and pop a per-class flag: rewrite them to pop `migrated_t205` instead, keeping what they prove.
- Every `assertEqual(…data['actions'], {})` / `assertFalse(…data['actions'])` (tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py :165 :192 :208 :416 :492 :514 :558 :563 :576 :597 :626 :652; tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py :84 :170 :221 :282 :326 :347 :479 :488 :498 :813 and the migration cases above; tests/lib/autopilot_sync.py :126 :174; not :214, which is a seed) becomes `assertNotIn('actions', …data)`. Indirect reads are rewritten the same way: tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py:604 (`for name in ('advanced', 'retries', 'wakes', 'actions')` in `test_authoritative_head_race_is_silent_and_next_observation_gates`, :601-608) drops 'actions' from the tuple and adds `assertNotIn('actions', self.pilot.data)`; tests/lib/autopilot_sync.py:221 (`assertNotIn(token, p.data['actions'])`) becomes `assertNotIn('actions', p.data)`. A grep of tests/ for `'actions'` and `data['actions']` after the change finds only the migration seeds, tests/lib/autopilot_reload.py having lost its case (below), and the unrelated tests/board-projects.test.sh:114.
- Reload idle check (tests/lib/autopilot_reload.py:323-340, `Rules.test_idle_and_identity`): drop the `actions` field from the fixture at :327, the `('actions', {'state':'started'})` case at :331 and the `actions=` entry in the `pilot.data.update(...)` at :336; the jobs, batches and wakes cases stay.
- Other `start_job` stubs that never assert one review per head (tests/lib/autopilot_turn.py:36, tests/lib/autopilot_task_resolution.py:75, tests/lib/preflight_lifecycle.py:133, tests/lib/run_project_turns.py:114) are checked and left unchanged. tests/lib/merge_authorization.py:105 (`self.p.once = lambda *args: None`) becomes dead once `once` is deleted: remove that line.

Docs, edited in place (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md):
- design/design.md §15.8 'Pilot and advanced integration' (starts :5255): the T-203 reload sentence at about :5293-5294 drops 'started actions'; the ledger paragraph at :5339-5375 replaces 'Review launch is the remaining write-ahead action class under `state/autopilot/` …' (:5360-5362) with the review-launch rule above (decided from the review job recorded for that PR head (at most one autopilot-launched review per head); a failed start marks the record uncertain and wakes once), and replaces the `migrated_t190`/`migrated_t193`/`migrated_t200`/`migrated_t204` sentences (:5356-5359, :5364-5366, :5368-5373) with one sentence on `migrated_t205` and the statement that the autopilot keeps no write-ahead action ledger; per-PR records (`updates`, `holds`, `advanced`, `rechecked`, `restacks`), shared `retries` and `jobs` remain.
- design/design.md §15.8 '#### Autopilot owns PR advancement (T-175)' (:5443): 'persist their cache and action identities across restarts' becomes 'persist their cache, per-PR records and jobs across restarts'.
- docs/autopilot.md: :18 drops 'started actions'; :58 'and other write-ahead action records' goes; :85-86 (review launch as the remaining write-ahead class) and :108-111 (the t190/t193 migration text) are rewritten to match the design text; the T-200/T-204 migration sentences (:81-84, :87-89) become one `migrated_t205` sentence.

Callers and mirrors (grep of `once(`, `['actions']`, `actions=`, `launch_review`, `launch-review`, `migrated_t190|t193|t200|t204`, `.recover()` and `'action-'` over bin/, tests/, board/, docs/, skills/ and design/design.md): production code is only bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py and bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py; tests are tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py, autopilot_cases.py, autopilot_sync.py, autopilot_reload.py, autopilot_jobs.py and merge_authorization.py (:105, a `once` stub, found by grepping `\.once\b` as well as `once(`) as listed above; tests/board-projects.test.sh:114 has an unrelated decision-file `actions` field and tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts uses EventEmitter `.once`, neither touched. No board, skill or script reads `state/autopilot/state.json`'s `actions`. bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py stays the only raiser listed beside bin/fm.sh in tests/decide.test.sh:983, and the new wake is queued through `self.queue`, not a card.

In flight. An autopilot already running pre-T-205 code keeps its `actions` map until it reloads: once firstmate fast-forwards main after this merges, T-203's reload drains it (jobs, batches, wakes; its own `reload_due` still also waits for started actions) and hands off; the new service runs the `migrated_t205` upgrade in `Pilot.__init__` before `recover()`. A review job started by the old code has no `kind` field and matches through its packet, and a not-done launch-review action without a job becomes an 'uncertain' review record in the migration, so the new code never launches a second autopilot review at a head the old code already tried. No other task in flight edits bin/lib/fm_autopilot*.py (T-190, T-193, T-200, T-203 and T-204 have merged).

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py (the job-record cases and the start-failure cases are red on base where `once()` decides; the stale-verdict case is a regression guard, green on base and head) and tests/lib/autopilot_cases.py (the `migrated_t205` cases are red on base); the `assertNotIn('actions', …)` rewrites are red on base where the key exists. No vendor stub is involved: the exceptions are raised by test stubs of `start_job`, as the existing stubs do.
